title: Team configuration for Claude Code
task_statement: Configure Claude Code for a team with committed settings, enforced rules, and guidance files. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Shared settings and scopes
components.first_principle: One committed settings file gives every clone the same permissions and hooks, and personal files hold the exceptions.
steps: Commit the shared settings file at .claude/settings.json in the repository.
Claude Code reads the user, shared project, project local, command line, and managed settings.
A key set at a higher level overrides the same key set at a lower level.
Managed settings take precedence over every other source.
Put personal exceptions in .claude/settings.local.json, which stays out of git.
Run /status to see which settings sources loaded for the session.
pros: Every clone receives the same permission rules and hooks after the commit.
Personal overrides need no commit and no change to the team file.
Managed settings apply on every machine that the organization deploys them to.
cons: A settings change reaches teammates only after the commit and a pull.
Settings files are strict JSON, so a comment or a trailing comma causes a Settings Error.
Some keys never take effect from a repository file, so a committed key can be ignored.
use_when: A team shares one repository and needs the same permission rules on every clone.
One developer needs an exception without a change to the team file.
do_not_use_when: A single session needs a temporary change, so the command line flag fits better.
The rule must hold on every machine, and a committed file cannot enforce it on machines that skip the commit.

constraints.choice: Commit .claude/settings.json with deny rules for secret reads and destructive commands.
constraints.combination: Add managed settings when the organization must enforce a rule on every developer machine.

constraints.choice: Put hooks that lint or test each edit in the shared settings file.
constraints.combination: Review each committed hook command like code, because a hook runs a shell command. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep credentials out of committed settings files. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Put a personal workspace key in the env block of the user settings file on one machine.

constraints.choice: Commit team skills in .claude/skills/ so every clone loads them.
constraints.combination: Use nested skill folders for code in a subdirectory of a monorepo.

native_services.text: The Bedrock setup wizard saves its result to the env block of the user settings file, not the shared project file.
Foundry has no setup wizard, so environment variables are the only configuration path.
A workspace API key takes precedence over SigV4 credentials, and the user settings env block can hold it on one machine.

components.exam_tie: D7.1. Expect a scenario where a team needs a control that holds on every clone. The credited answer uses permissions, hooks, or managed settings in a file that the team shares. (Inference)
components.trap: A CLAUDE.md note that asks the agent not to read secret files. The docs call CLAUDE.md context, not enforced configuration, so only a deny rule blocks the read.
components.decision_rule: Use a permission rule or a hook for a control, and use CLAUDE.md for a convention.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario needs a block, choose a deny rule, a PreToolUse hook, or managed settings.

key_facts.text: Claude Code reads settings from four files: user, shared project, project local, and managed.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Settings precedence runs from managed settings down to user settings, with the command line between managed and project local.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Permission rules evaluate in this order: deny, then ask, then allow.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A deny rule in any settings scope blocks a call that another scope allows.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A PreToolUse hook that exits with code 2 blocks the tool call before permission rules run.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Keep each CLAUDE.md file under 200 lines.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Permission rules and hooks
components.first_principle: Permission rules and hooks decide a tool call in code, so the result does not depend on what the model chooses.

nodes.label: PostToolUse hook runs lint or tests

steps: The model requests a tool call, such as an edit or a shell command.
PreToolUse hooks run before the permission prompt.
Claude Code evaluates deny rules first, then ask rules, then allow rules.
A deny rule for the call blocks it, even when a hook returns allow.
A PostToolUse hook runs after the tool call succeeds, for example to lint the edited file.
pros: A deny rule holds even when the model wants to run the blocked command.
A hook runs the same check on every machine that has the committed file.
Rules name the tool, so the team can review them in one file. (Inference)
cons: A Bash rule matches the command text, so another form of the same program can pass.
A command hook runs shell code, so a bad hook can change files on every clone. (Inference)
A stalled PreToolUse hook does not block a call by default.
use_when: A destructive command must never run in any session in the repository.
Every edit must trigger a lint or test command.
do_not_use_when: The rule is a style preference, so CLAUDE.md is the better place.
The control must cover every process on the machine, so a sandbox is the better layer.

constraints.choice: Deny secret file reads with Read rules in the shared settings file.
constraints.combination: Add the same rule to managed settings when the organization requires it on every machine.

constraints.choice: Use a PostToolUse hook with an Edit or Write matcher for lint.
constraints.combination: Use a PreToolUse hook with onFailure set to block when a failed check must stop the call.

constraints.choice: Use one deny rule for a path pattern instead of one rule per file.
constraints.combination: Use an ask rule for the gray cases that need a person to decide.

constraints.choice: Restrict subagent tools with the tools field in the agent file.

components.exam_tie: D7.1. Expect a scenario that asks how to block a tool or run a check on every edit. The credited answer uses a deny rule or a hook, not a prompt instruction. (Inference)
components.trap: A PreToolUse hook that returns allow, which looks like approval. A deny rule still blocks the call, so the hook does not override the team policy.
components.decision_rule: Use a deny rule to block a tool and a hook to run a check at a lifecycle event.
components.exam_tip: If the stem says the model must not run a command, choose the deny rule over a note in the memory file.

key_facts.text: Permission rules evaluate in this order: deny, then ask, then allow.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A PreToolUse hook decision does not bypass a deny rule.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A PreToolUse hook that exits with code 2 blocks the tool call before permission rules run.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The default timeout for a command hook is 600 seconds.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Read and Edit deny rules apply to built-in file tools and to file commands that Bash recognizes.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The sandbox adds OS-level enforcement that Read rules alone do not give.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: On PreToolUse, a timed-out command hook does not block the tool call unless onFailure is set to block.
key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: CLAUDE.md and subagent guidance
components.first_principle: Guidance files shape how the model works, and they cannot stop a tool call.
steps: Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md files from the current directory and its parents at launch.
Claude reads the CLAUDE.md content and tries to follow it.
A subagent file sets a tools field that limits the tools the subagent can use.
Permission rules still decide every tool call the subagent makes.
Move a control that must hold into a permission rule or a hook.
pros: CLAUDE.md is fast to write and shapes style and conventions.
A subagent with a read-only tools list cannot write files.
Team files are committed, so every clone gets the same guidance.
cons: A CLAUDE.md line gives no guarantee of compliance, especially for vague instructions.
A long CLAUDE.md file uses more context and reduces adherence.
Plugin subagents do not support the hooks, mcpServers, or permissionMode fields.
use_when: The team wants a style convention that the model follows across sessions.
A research task needs a subagent that only reads files.
do_not_use_when: The rule must block an action, because a note cannot stop a tool call.
The guidance applies to one folder only and a path-scoped rule file fits better.

constraints.choice: Use CLAUDE.md for behavior guidance and settings for enforcement.
constraints.combination: Deploy a managed CLAUDE.md file when every user needs the same guidance.

constraints.choice: Split long guidance into files under .claude/rules/.
constraints.combination: Add a paths field to a rule file so it loads only for files that match.

constraints.choice: Put a repeatable workflow in a skill folder under .claude/skills/.
constraints.combination: Use the skill description so the model loads the skill when the task matches.

constraints.choice: Give a research subagent only the Read and Grep tools.
constraints.combination: Name the subagent in the agents folder so the team can invoke it by name.

components.exam_tie: D7.1. Expect a scenario that mixes a convention with a security need. The credited answer keeps the convention in CLAUDE.md and moves the security need to settings. (Inference)
components.trap: A bigger model with a long CLAUDE.md file, expected to enforce a secret rule. Adherence to guidance is not a lock, so the rule belongs in permissions.
components.decision_rule: Write a convention in CLAUDE.md, and write a required block in a permission rule.
components.exam_tip: If an answer relies on the model to follow a note for safety, reject it and look for a deny rule.

key_facts.text: Claude treats CLAUDE.md files as context, not enforced configuration.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Keep each CLAUDE.md file under 200 lines.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A subagent without a tools field inherits every tool available to subagents.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Managed subagent definitions take precedence over project and user subagents with the same name.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Plugin subagents do not support the hooks, mcpServers, or permissionMode frontmatter fields.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Project skills load from .claude/skills/ and commit with the repository.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Must the rule hold even if the model disagrees?} -->|No| G[Convention in CLAUDE.md]
  A -->|Yes| B{Is the control a tool permission?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Deny or ask rule in settings]
  B -->|No| D[Hook at a lifecycle event]
  C --> E{Must every developer machine enforce it?}
  E -->|Yes| F[Managed settings]
  E -->|No| H[Committed shared settings file]
  D --> H
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  M[Managed file] --> P[Permission check]
  S[Shared file in repo] --> P
  L[Local file] --> P
  S --> K[Hooks]
  P --> X[Deny beats allow]
  G[CLAUDE.md] --> Z[Guidance only]
  T[Subagent tools list] --> Y[Read only]
